answer: An operator running 57 keys thus pays for 57 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Because the oasis salt is published after the umber checkpoint, the ferrous audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 193 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 26 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
